title: Jude
subtitle: The Letter of Jude - Key Notes, Cross-References, and Messianic Connections (WEB)

items.value: Jude is twenty-five verses, written by a brother of Yahshua who calls himself His servant. He meant to write about the salvation they shared and wrote instead a call to contend for the faith once for all delivered.
It is one of the sternest letters in the Bible, and it ends with one of the most beautiful doxologies.

sections.heading: How this study is put together

items.value: Each of the shortest books in the Bible is one chapter long, so each one is a complete study in a single guide, laid out the same way as every other book in this series.

values: **Key Notes** - observations worth having in hand before you read, each ending with the verses it comes from.
**Key Cross-References** - passages that stand behind or alongside the text, grouped by theme.
**Messianic Connections** - places where the text reaches back into the Hebrew Scriptures or points ahead to the Messiah. Where an entry is a pattern rather than a prediction, the note says so.
**For Further Study** - places to go deeper.
**Introduction** - the book read as a whole before you read it in parts.
**The text itself**, printed in full in the World English Bible, with footnote markers on the verses the references belong to.

items.value: Every scripture reference is a live link to the World English Bible on BibleGateway. In the app, tapping a footnote marker shows the full text of the passages cited and a line on why they connect.

sections.heading: A note on the divine names

items.value: In the notes and introductions this study uses **Yahweh** for the covenant name of God and **Yahshua** for the Messiah. The printed scripture text is never altered; the World English Bible stands exactly as the translators set it, so our own speech and the translator's work stay visibly distinct.

Jude is Judah, one of the brothers of Yahshua named in Mark 6, and the brother of James. Like James, he never calls himself the Lord's brother, only His servant - which is all the more striking because the brothers did not believe in Him during His ministry.

Jude draws on the Hebrew Scriptures throughout - the Exodus, Sodom, Cain, Balaam, Korah, Zechariah 3 - and also on two Jewish works his readers knew. The dispute between Michael and the devil over Moses' body is said by early writers to come from the Assumption of Moses, and the prophecy of Enoch matches the opening of the book of Enoch. Jude quotes them as true words, the way Paul quotes Greek poets, without calling either book Scripture.

Jude 6 connects the angels who left their dwelling with Sodom's going after strange flesh. Many from the earliest readers on have linked it with the sons of God of Genesis 6, and this study reads it that way.

values: **Verses 1-4** - greeting, and why he had to write: men who turned grace into license.
**Verses 5-16** - warnings from the whole of Scripture, and a portrait of the false teachers.
**Verses 17-23** - remember, build, pray, keep yourselves, and have mercy.
**Verses 24-25** - Him who is able to keep you from stumbling.

chapters.heading: JUDE - Contend for the Faith, Wandering Stars, and Him Who Is Able to Keep You
chapters.title: Contend for the Faith, Wandering Stars, and Him Who Is Able to Keep You
keyNotes: Jude is Judah, one of the brothers of Yahshua named in the Gospels. James, the brother he names, led the assembly in Jerusalem. Neither ever calls himself the Lord's brother. Both call themselves His servant (Jude 1:1, Mark 6:3).

The brothers who did not believe in Him while He walked among them became His servants after He rose. Jude is living proof that unbelief at the family table is not the end of the story (Jude 1:1, John 7:5).

"Called, sanctified by God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ." Kept appears at the start and again at the end: kept for Him, keep yourselves in God's love, and Him who is able to keep you (Jude 1:1, 1:21, 1:24).
He had planned a letter about our common salvation and was constrained to write this one instead. Sometimes the letter you want to write is not the letter that is needed (Jude 1:3).
"Contend earnestly" is an athlete's or a wrestler's word, the effort of a contest. Not quarrel - contend (Jude 1:3).
"The faith which was once for all delivered to the saints." Delivered once, and complete. Nothing new needs to be added to it, and nothing taken away (Jude 1:3, Deuteronomy 4:2).
"Certain men who crept in secretly." They came in through the side door. False teachers rarely announce themselves at the front (Jude 1:4).

"Turning the grace of our God into indecency." Grace treated as permission to live without restraint. Grace was never meant to set aside obedience; it is what makes obedience possible (Jude 1:4, Titus 2:11-12).
"Denying our only Master, God, and Lord, Jesus Christ." Master here is despotes, the word for an owner. They did not deny His existence. They denied His authority over how they lived (Jude 1:4).

"The Lord, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt." Some of the oldest manuscripts read Jesus here - Yahshua saved a people out of Egypt. The WEB reads the Lord. Either way, the one who brought Israel out is the one Jude serves (Jude 1:5, Exodus 20:2).
A whole generation was saved out of Egypt and still died in the wilderness because they did not believe. Being delivered once does not make continuing in unbelief safe (Jude 1:5, Numbers 14:29-30).

"Angels who didn't keep their first domain, but deserted their own dwelling place." Many, from the earliest Jewish and Christian readers on, connect this with the sons of God in Genesis 6 who took human wives, and Kingdom Life reads it that way (Jude 1:6, Genesis 6:2, 6:4).

"Even as Sodom and Gomorrah... in the same way as these." The comparison is to the angels just named. Both crossed a boundary God had set: the angels left their place, and Sodom went after strange flesh (Jude 1:6-7, Genesis 19:4-5).
"Strange flesh" is literally other flesh, flesh of a different kind. The men of Sodom were demanding the angelic visitors in Lot's house (Jude 1:7, Genesis 19:5).
"In their dreaming" - they claim visions as their authority. Dreams are the source; the flesh is the result (Jude 1:8, Deuteronomy 13:1-3).

Michael the archangel disputing with the devil over Moses' body is not told in the Hebrew Scriptures, which say only that Yahweh buried Moses and no one knows where. Early writers say Jude drew it from a Jewish work called the Assumption of Moses (Jude 1:9, Deuteronomy 34:5-6).

"May the Lord rebuke you" are the very words spoken to Satan in Zechariah 3, over Joshua the high priest. Even the archangel left the rebuke to Yahweh. If Michael would not speak abusively about the devil, no man has license to (Jude 1:9, Zechariah 3:2).
Michael's name means who is like El? It is a question, and the answer is no one - which is exactly why he would not presume (Jude 1:9).

Three men, three ways to go wrong. Cain, who murdered his brother out of envy. Balaam, who sold his gift for hire and taught Israel to sin at Peor. Korah, who rose up against the authority Yahweh had set (Jude 1:11, Genesis 4:8, Numbers 31:16, 16:31-33).
"Hidden rocky reefs in your love feasts." The love feasts were the meals the believers shared. A reef is invisible from the surface until the ship is on it (Jude 1:12).
"Shepherds who without fear feed themselves" is Ezekiel 34: woe to the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves instead of the sheep (Jude 1:12, Ezekiel 34:2).
Clouds without water promise rain and deliver nothing. Proverbs says the same of a man who boasts of a gift he never gives (Jude 1:12, Proverbs 25:14).
"Autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots." Fruitless at the very season fruit is expected, dead, and uprooted (Jude 1:12, Matthew 7:19).
"Wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame." Isaiah: the wicked are like the troubled sea that cannot rest, casting up mire and mud (Jude 1:13, Isaiah 57:20).
"Wandering stars" - lights that do not hold their course and so cannot guide anyone home (Jude 1:13).

Enoch, the seventh from Adam, is quoted here. The words match the opening of the book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish writing. Jude quotes it the way Paul quotes Greek poets: a true word, from a source not otherwise counted as Scripture. Jude does not call the whole book Scripture (Jude 1:14-15).

"Behold, the Lord came with ten thousands of his holy ones." Moses said Yahweh came from Sinai with ten thousands of holy ones, and Zechariah: Yahweh my God will come, and all the holy ones with you (Jude 1:14, Deuteronomy 33:2, Zechariah 14:5).
Ungodly, in one form or another, appears four times in one verse. Jude is not being subtle (Jude 1:15).
"Murmurers and complainers" - the wilderness word again, the sin of the generation that came out of Egypt (Jude 1:16, Numbers 14:27).
"Their mouth speaks proud things." Pride again, in the mouth (Jude 1:16).
"Remember the words which have been spoken before by the apostles." The answer to new teaching is old teaching, remembered (Jude 1:17, 2 Peter 3:3).
"Sensual, not having the Spirit." For all their claims of dreams and visions, they lack the one thing that matters (Jude 1:19).
Four instructions for the faithful: build yourselves up on the faith, pray in the Holy Spirit, keep yourselves in God's love, and look for the mercy of the Lord (Jude 1:20-21).
"Keep yourselves in God's love." Not make God love you - keep yourselves where His love is (Jude 1:21, John 15:9-10).

Three kinds of people to help: those who doubt, to whom you show mercy; those already in the fire, whom you snatch out; and those you help with fear, hating even the garment stained by the flesh (Jude 1:22-23).

"Snatching them out of the fire" is Zechariah 3 again: is this not a burning stick plucked out of the fire? And there Joshua's filthy garments were taken off him and he was clothed in rich clothing (Jude 1:23, Zechariah 3:2-4).
"Him who is able to keep them from stumbling." After a whole letter of people who fell, the last word is the One who keeps (Jude 1:24, Psalm 121:3).
"To present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy." Faultless is the word used of a sacrifice without blemish. He presents us that way, and He does it with joy (Jude 1:24).
"To God our Savior, who alone is wise." Isaiah: there is no other God besides me, a just God and a Savior (Jude 1:25, Isaiah 45:21).

intro: Jude's letter runs to twenty-five verses and was written by Judah, one of the brothers of Yahshua named in Mark 6 - one of the brothers who, according to John 7, did not believe in Him while He walked among them. He introduces himself not as the Lord's brother but as His servant. He had meant to write about the salvation he and his readers shared, and found himself compelled instead to urge them to contend for the faith once for all delivered to the saints, because men had crept in unnoticed who turned the grace of God into license and denied the authority of their only Master.

He reminds them of what they already know. A people saved out of Egypt - by Jesus, in some of the oldest manuscripts - were destroyed in the wilderness for unbelief. Angels who abandoned their proper dwelling, whom many from the earliest readers onward identify with the sons of God of Genesis 6, are kept in darkness for judgment, and Sodom in the same way pursued strange flesh. Against men who slander celestial beings he sets Michael the archangel, who in disputing with the devil over Moses' body left the rebuke to Yahweh, in the words Zechariah records. Then come Cain's envy, Balaam's greed and Korah's rebellion, and a sequence of images: reefs hidden at the love feasts, rainless clouds, fruitless trees twice dead, wild waves, wandering stars. He quotes the prophecy attributed to Enoch, of the Lord coming with ten thousands of His holy ones, as Moses and Zechariah had also said.

Then he turns to the faithful. They are to build themselves up in the faith, pray in the Holy Spirit, keep themselves in God's love, and wait for the Lord's mercy; to show mercy to the doubting, snatch others from the fire as Joshua the high priest was plucked from it and stripped of his filthy garments, and keep themselves clean while they do it. And he ends not with the warning but with the One who is able to keep them from stumbling and to present them faultless before His glory with great joy - God our Savior, who alone is wise.

verses.1: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to those who are called, sanctified by God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ:
verses.2: Mercy to you and peace and love be multiplied.
verses.3: Beloved, while I was very eager to write to you about our common salvation, I was constrained to write to you exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints.
verses.4: For there are certain men who crept in secretly, even those who were long ago written about for this condemnation: ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into indecency, and denying our only Master, God, and Lord, Jesus Christ.
verses.5: Now I desire to remind you, though you already know this, that the Lord, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who didn’t believe.
verses.6: Angels who didn’t keep their first domain, but deserted their own dwelling place, he has kept in everlasting bonds under darkness for the judgment of the great day.
verses.7: Even as Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities around them, having, in the same way as these, given themselves over to sexual immorality and gone after strange flesh, are shown as an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire.
verses.8: Yet in the same way, these also in their dreaming defile the flesh, despise authority, and slander celestial beings.
verses.9: But Michael, the archangel, when contending with the devil and arguing about the body of Moses, dared not bring against him an abusive condemnation, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you!”
verses.10: But these speak evil of whatever things they don’t know. They are destroyed in these things that they understand naturally, like the creatures without reason.
verses.11: Woe to them! For they went in the way of Cain, and ran riotously in the error of Balaam for hire, and perished in Korah’s rebellion.
verses.12: These are hidden rocky reefs in your love feasts when they feast with you, shepherds who without fear feed themselves; clouds without water, carried along by winds; autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots;
verses.13: wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever.
verses.14: About these also Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, “Behold, the Lord came with ten thousands of his holy ones,
verses.15: to execute judgment on all, and to convict all the ungodly of all their works of ungodliness which they have done in an ungodly way, and of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.”
verses.16: These are murmurers and complainers, walking after their lusts (and their mouth speaks proud things), showing respect of persons to gain advantage.
verses.17: But you, beloved, remember the words which have been spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.18: They said to you that “In the last time there will be mockers, walking after their own ungodly lusts.”
verses.19: These are they who cause divisions, and are sensual, not having the Spirit.
verses.20: But you, beloved, keep building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit.
verses.21: Keep yourselves in God’s love, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to eternal life.
verses.22: On some have compassion, making a distinction,
verses.23: and some save, snatching them out of the fire with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.
verses.24: Now to him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy,
verses.25: to God our Savior, who alone is wise, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and forever. Amen.

cites.text: You shall not add to the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it, that you may keep the commandments of Yahweh your God which I command you.
“Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to those who take refuge in him. Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.

3.why: you shall not add to the word nor take from it, and do not add to his words, lest he reprove you

cites.text: “I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
“Yet I am Yahweh your God from the land of Egypt; and you shall acknowledge no god but me, and besides me there is no savior.

5.why: I am Yahweh your God who brought you out of Egypt, and besides me there is no savior

cites.text: Your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness; and all who were counted of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, who have murmured against me, surely you shall not come into the land, concerning which I swore that I would make you dwell therein, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.
However with most of them, God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness.

5.why: your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness, and most of them were overthrown in the wilderness

cites.text: God’s sons saw that men’s daughters were beautiful, and they took any that they wanted for themselves as wives.
The Nephilim were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when God’s sons came in to men’s daughters and had children with them. Those were the mighty men who were of old, men of renown.

6.why: the sons of God taking the daughters of men as wives, and the Nephilim in the earth in those days

cites.text: But before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, both young and old, all the people from every quarter. They called to Lot, and said to him, “Where are the men who came in to you this night? Bring them out to us, that we may have sex with them.”
Then Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from Yahweh out of the sky.

7.why: the men of Sodom surrounding Lot's house for the visitors, and sulfur and fire rained from Yahweh

cites.text: Yahweh said to Satan, “Yahweh rebuke you, Satan! Yes, Yahweh who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Isn’t this a burning stick plucked out of the fire?”

So Moses the servant of Yahweh died there in the land of Moab, according to Yahweh’s word. He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth Peor, but no man knows where his tomb is to this day.

9.why: Yahweh rebuke you, Satan, and Moses buried in Moab with no man knowing his tomb

cites.text: but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell. Yahweh said to Cain, “Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen? If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.” Cain said to Abel, his brother, “Let’s go into the field.” While they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel, his brother, and killed him.
Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahweh in the matter of Peor, and so the plague was among the congregation of Yahweh.

As he finished speaking all these words, the ground that was under them split apart. The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households, all of Korah’s men, and all their goods. So they, and all that belonged to them went down alive into Sheol. The earth closed on them, and they perished from among the assembly.

11.why: Cain rising up against Abel, the counsel of Balaam at Peor, and the earth swallowing Korah's men

cites.text: As clouds and wind without rain, so is he who boasts of gifts deceptively.

“Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy, and tell them, even the shepherds, ‘Thus says the Lord Yahweh: “Woe to the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves! Shouldn’t the shepherds feed the sheep?

12.why: clouds and wind without rain, and woe to the shepherds who feed themselves

cites.text: But the wicked are like the troubled sea; for it can’t rest, and its waters cast up mire and mud.

13.why: the wicked are like the troubled sea, casting up mire and mud

cites.text: He said, “Yahweh came from Sinai, and rose from Seir to them. He shone from Mount Paran. He came from the ten thousands of holy ones. At his right hand was a fiery law for them.

You shall flee by the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach to Azel; yes, you shall flee, just like you fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Yahweh my God will come, and all the holy ones with you.

14.why: Yahweh came from the ten thousands of holy ones, and Yahweh my God will come, and all the holy ones with you

cites.text: For, behold, Yahweh will come with fire, and his chariots will be like the whirlwind; to render his anger with fierceness, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For Yahweh will execute judgment by fire and by his sword on all flesh; and those slain by Yahweh will be many.

15.why: Yahweh will come with fire and execute judgment on all flesh

cites.text: Yahweh said to Satan, “Yahweh rebuke you, Satan! Yes, Yahweh who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Isn’t this a burning stick plucked out of the fire?”
“I have overthrown some of you, as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a burning stick plucked out of the fire; yet you haven’t returned to me,” says Yahweh.

23.why: a burning stick plucked out of the fire

cites.text: Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and was standing before the angel. He answered and spoke to those who stood before him, saying, “Take the filthy garments off him.” To him he said, “Behold, I have caused your iniquity to pass from you, and I will clothe you with rich clothing.”
For we have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is like a polluted garment. We all fade like a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.

23.why: the filthy garments taken off and rich clothing put on, and our righteousness like a polluted garment

cites.text: He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber.
Though he stumble, he shall not fall, for Yahweh holds him up with his hand.

24.why: he will not allow your foot to be moved, and though he stumble he shall not fall

cites.text: Declare and present it. Yes, let them take counsel together. Who has shown this from ancient time? Who has declared it of old? Haven’t I, Yahweh? There is no other God besides me, a just God and a Savior; There is no one besides me.
I myself am Yahweh; and besides me there is no savior.

25.why: a just God and a Savior, there is no one besides me, and besides me there is no savior
